Subject: RE: Spike: 429s & steady latency increase since 08:45 PDT

Naomi / Liam — quick technical summary after initial triage.

Findings (TL;DR):
- We observed an "eviction-loop" pattern in the dedicated GPU pool where autoscaler and our eviction heuristics interacted unexpectedly: nodes were marked for eviction during warmup, freed, then immediately re-requested by the allocator which caused a cycle of warmup -> eviction -> re-add. This produced sustained allocation churn and left requests queued until capacity stabilized.
- The trace file (eviction-trace-20260908.log) shows repeated preemption windows at 08:43–09:05 with a 30–45s wall time between reclaim and reallocation for the affected nodes.
- External causes: no config changes detected on NovaStream side; traffic pattern was steady. Root cause is a race in our warmup window + eviction-threshold tuning on the Dedicated autoscaler.

Short-term mitigations we applied at 09:00 PDT (already in effect):
1) Disabled aggressive warmup-triggered evictions for the affected pool for 30 minutes (falls back to conservative policy).
2) Enabled CPU-backed fallback instances for the lowest-latency tier to absorb short bursts (gradual cutover; documented risk: slight latency increase for a subset of requests).
3) Applied a temporary client-side 10% ingress limit for NovaStream (opt-in) while we stabilize to avoid wasteful retries.

Attached: eviction trace and a small patch with the mitigation toggles (eviction-loop-mitigation.patch).

Longer-term next steps (postmortem items):
- Adjust warmup/eviction interaction and add a short lock to prevent immediate reallocation within the same eviction window.
- Add a canary that exercises warmup+eviction interactions before policy rollouts.
- Improve runbook to include immediate CPU-fallback + ingestion throttles.

We'll schedule a postmortem early next week and share a draft RCA and timeline. Ben — can you confirm the customer comms and credit proposal?

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Liam — following up with a concise customer-facing summary and next steps.

Summary of impact:
- Incident window: 08:43–09:12 PDT (transient churn visible through 09:05).
- Symptoms: elevated 429s, queued requests, throughput ~40% of baseline for ~20 minutes.
- Root cause (prelim): allocator/eviction race causing repeated node churn in dedicated pool.

What we did for NovaStream (already completed):
- Stabilized pool by disabling aggressive eviction warmups.
- Brought up CPU-backed fallback to reduce 429s while preserving throughput.
- Limited ingress by 10% to prevent retries from amplifying the issue.

Customer-facing asks and offers:
- We will run a full RCA and deliver a formal postmortem by EOD Monday 2026-09-13 with a timeline for the code fix.
- As goodwill for the disruption we will: 1) credit one week of Dedicated usage proportional to the impacted time window, 2) offer a one-hour technical review with Karthik + runtime team to walk the fix and preventive controls.
- If helpful, we can also schedule an ad-hoc runbook walkthrough with your SREs this week.

Next operational steps (owner):
- Karthik: produce a patch for warmup/eviction race and a canary plan (ETA: 2026-09-10).
- Marissa: coordinate credit and formal comms (customer-friendly postmortem + promotion of fallback options).
- Naomi: executive touchpoint if NovaStream requests additional escalation.

Liam — want to confirm you received the artifacts (trace + snapshot) and whether the 10% ingress reduction worked on your end. If you want a short sync today, we can carve out 30 minutes.

Thanks again for partnering closely; we appreciate the prompt reports which helped narrow this quickly.
